Entries.Text: Weapons can only be assigned to the player character (c0000).
Ctrl+click or Shift+click clips in the Clips list to pick several: a change here is then made to all of them, as one undo step.
The clips picked in the Clips list. A plain click there picks one again.
Plays every picked clip faster or slower (offset keys folded in, as the Clip tool's Speed). Their time act events aren't retimed: the check before Export lists any that then start past a clip's end.
Scales the root motion of every picked clip that has some (ground travel, up and down, turn; 0 removes it), keeping the bones' keys. Clips without root motion are passed over.
Keys the offsets copied from {0} frame {1} on every picked clip at this frame (a shorter clip's last), by bone name. E.g. copy a shield arm fix once, then paste it on every guard animation.
Some picked clips have no track for: {0}. Those offsets weren't pasted there.
Batch: {0} clips changed, {1} passed over (unreadable, or nothing to change).
Root motion x{1} / x{2} / x{3} on {0} clips
Paste {0} offsets on {1} clips at frame {2}
Only the clips the game uses: with a time act entry, played by another entry (its HKX imported), or named in the character's behavior files. Clips with work and new IDs always show.
Neither the time acts nor the behaviors of this character could be read, so every clip shows.
Couldn't read the behaviors in {0} to tell which clips are used.

Keep the work of every edited clip (its frames, and its offset keys apart from them) in the project's .smithbox/Animations folder. The anibnds aren't written: use Export for that. The keys can be edited again in a later session.

Bake the work (keys included) of every clip not exported yet into its anibnd in the project, add the new IDs and take the deleted clips out. The work is saved too and kept, so the keys stay editable and can be exported again. The character is read again afterwards, so the undo history is cleared.
No character in this project has an anibnd.
{0} has no animations this editor can read.
Failed to open the animations of {0}
{1} has no clip {0} in the Animation Editor.
Selects this clip's time act entry in the Time Act Editor, to see or edit its events.
This clip's ID has no time act entry (a new ID gets one with Make Time Act Entry), or the time acts haven't been read yet.
{0} has edited clips whose work isn't saved. Opening {1} drops it unless it is saved first (saving doesn't write the anibnds).
Select a character to list its clips.
Plays the animations of {0}. Exporting edits them for every character that shares them.
Copy this clip, as it is now, under a new ID in the same anibnd. Listed as (new) until exported. Can be undone.
The name of the copy of {0} (aXXX_YYYYYY):
Move this clip to another ID. On Export, the file is written under the new ID and the old one is taken out of the anibnd. Time acts and behaviors that use the old ID are not changed. Can be undone.
Take this clip out of its anibnd on Export. Time acts and behaviors that use it are not changed. Can be undone.
Select a clip to play and edit it.
{0} can't be decoded by this editor.
The selected clip. Edits play in the viewport straight away. Save keeps them, keys apart, in the project's .smithbox/Animations folder; Export bakes them into the anibnd.
Saved, not exported to the anibnd
New ID, saved, not exported to the anibnd
Additive: played on top of another animation
One frame back (Left Arrow while the Timeline is focused)
One frame on (Right Arrow while the Timeline is focused)
Play or pause the clip in the viewport (Space while the Timeline is focused). Root motion isn't applied: the character plays in place.
How fast the clip plays in the viewport. This doesn't change the clip: use Speed in the Clip tool for that.
Frame {0}. Click or drag to go there. Yellow marks are the selected bone's keys, grey ones other bones' keys.
Starts after the clip's last frame, so it never plays. Move it in the Time Act Editor.
This animation has no time act entry, so it has no events.
This animation's time act entry has no events.
Reads the character's time acts again, after saving them in the Time Act Editor. Unsaved Time Act Editor edits aren't seen here.
The clip's timing changed (length x{0}, shifted {1} frames). Its time act events still have the old timing.

Moves the clip's time act events the same way in the Time Act Editor, as one step of its undo history. Events that would no longer play (wholly before the start or after the end) are removed. Save the time acts there to keep it. Undo here doesn't undo it there.
Keeps the time act events as they are. Move them yourself in the Time Act Editor if needed.
This animation has no time act entry to retime.
Its events are imported from {0}, which other animations may use too, so they aren't retimed from here.
Sent to the Time Act Editor. Save the time acts there, then Read Time Acts Again on the Timeline to see them here.
The bones of {0}'s model couldn't be read, so the clip can't be shown on it.
Each operation makes a new version of the clip, which can be undone. Root motion is edited with the poses.
Keep only the frames from First to Last (both kept). The root motion starts from zero again at the new first frame.

Play the clip faster or slower: 2 is twice as fast (half the frames), 0.5 half as fast. The root covers the same distance in the new time.

Time act events keep their times, so they may need moving in the Time Act Editor.
A bone turns {0} degrees between two frames of this clip. At this speed that becomes {1} degrees, past 180, so it would turn the short way round (a fast spin would go backwards).
Play the clip over this many frames, at the same frame rate. The same as Speed, given as a length.
Play the clip backwards. The root goes back along its path from where the clip ended.
Swap the character's left and right sides: each L_ bone takes its R_ bone's motion, mirrored, and the other way round. The root turns the other way.
An additive clip can't be mirrored.
{0} animated bones have a mirror bone this clip doesn't animate, so their motion is lost when mirrored. Hover to see them.
More clips match: filter to find one.
Play the picked clip after this one. Over the blend frames, the end of this clip crossfades into the start of the picked one, and the root carries on from where this clip left it.
The picked clip doesn't animate the same bones in the same order, so it can't be appended.
The picked clip has different float tracks, so it can't be appended.
One clip is additive and the other isn't, so they can't be joined.
Drop this clip's work (edits and keys), back to the clip as its anibnd has it. Saving then removes its work files. Can be undone.
How opaque the character's mesh is drawn. Lower it to see the skeleton through the body. Only the viewport is affected.
Draw the clip's root motion path (green): where the root goes over the clip from the origin, a mark each second, and an arrow at the playing frame showing where the character faces.
Move the character along its root motion while it plays, as the game does, instead of playing in place. The skeleton, bone picking and the gizmo follow it.
This clip has no root motion: the game doesn't move the character while it plays. Add it below.

For a clip whose character moves away from where it starts by moving its root bone: that travel becomes root motion, and the bone keeps the rest. With the root motion applied (in game, or Travel in the Configuration tool) the character looks the same, but the game now moves it.
No bone can give root motion: it needs an animated bone whose parents the clip doesn't animate (normally Master).
The bone whose travel becomes root motion. Master, the skeleton's root, moves the whole character.
The bone's turn about up becomes root motion too, so the game turns the character.
The bone's up and down movement becomes root motion too (a jump). Off, it stays in the bone and the root stays on the ground.
Move the bone's travel into root motion. Can be undone.
For a clip that plays in place: how far the game moves and turns the character over the clip. The poses don't change, so the character slides unless the clip was made to travel.
How far the character travels the way it faces, over the whole clip. Negative goes backwards.
How far the character travels to its right. Negative goes left.
How far the character rises (negative: falls) over the clip.
How far the character turns over the clip, in degrees. Positive turns right, negative left.
Linear travels at an even speed; Smooth starts and ends gently.
Give the clip this root motion. Can be undone.
Root motion path for {0} ({1} forward, {2} deg turn)
How far the clip moves the character by its last frame.
Multiply each part of the root motion. The poses stay as they are, so a large change makes the feet slide.
How far the character travels along the ground, times this: 1.2 makes a lunge go a fifth further, 0 keeps it in place.
How far the character moves up or down, times this: 0 keeps it on the ground.
How far the character turns, times this: 0 keeps its facing, -1 turns it the other way.
Scale the root motion by the three values. Can be undone.
Common root motion changes in one click, each undoable.
Remove the up and down part of the root motion, keeping the character on the ground.
Keep the character facing the way it started, while still travelling.
The clip plays in place: the character doesn't move or turn while it plays.
The path is drawn in the viewport (Configuration tool > Show Root Path); Configuration > Travel moves the character along it while playing.
Select the root motion (Root Motion in the Bones tool), so the viewport gizmo and the key fields key it as they do a bone: add height, sideways movement or a turn at the playing frame.
{0} root key(s), included in the figures above. Scaling, flattening or removing folds them into the root motion.

The root rises {0} m (frames {1}-{2}), but this clip's time act never disables gravity, so in game the character stays on the ground. Add a Disable Gravity flag (ChrActionFlag) over those frames in the Time Act Editor.

The root rises {0} m (frames {1}-{2}), but the time act disables gravity over only part of that (frames {3}), so in game the character is pulled back down early. Extend the Disable Gravity flag (ChrActionFlag) over the climb in the Time Act Editor.
The root rises {0} m (frames {1}-{2}), but this clip has no time act. It needs one with a Disable Gravity flag (ChrActionFlag) over those frames to lift the character in game.

In game the character is held to the ground unless its time act disables gravity, so vertical root motion only lifts it while gravity is off. Vanilla clips turn gravity off from the start of the rise and back on shortly before landing. A few vanilla clips rise without it and are moved by other means (ladder and lift moves, some enemy jumps with InvokeHeightCorrection), so this is a guide rather than a rule. Checked against the time acts as saved in the project.
Read this character's time acts again, after saving changes in the Time Act Editor.
{0} of the clips to export may not work as expected in game. Export anyway, or pick a clip to fix it first.
Selects this clip and closes this prompt, so it can be fixed before exporting.
Exports every clip as it is, warnings and all. The work files are kept, so the clips can still be fixed and exported again.
The root rises (frames {0}-{1}) but its time act never disables gravity, so in game the character stays on the ground.
The root rises (frames {0}-{1}) but its time act disables gravity over only part of the climb.
{0} time act events start after the clip's last frame ({1}), so they never play.
The clip's timing changed, but its time act events weren't retimed (Retime Time Act Events in the Clip tool).
This new animation has no time act entry yet: without one it has no events (attacks, sounds, cancel windows) and may not play in game. Make one in the Time Act Editor.

Adds a ChrActionFlag Disable Gravity event to this animation's time act in the Time Act Editor, as one step of its undo history: from frame 0 to the last frame the root is still up, so gravity takes over for the landing, as vanilla clips do. Save the time acts there to keep it, then Check Again.
This animation's events are imported from {0}, which other animations may use too, so the event isn't added from here.
Disable Gravity sent to the Time Act Editor. Save the time acts there, then Check Again.
Animation Editor: couldn't read the time acts of {0} for the gravity check.
Animation Editor: couldn't read the time act templates for the gravity check.
Scale root motion of {0} (ground x{1}, vertical x{2}, turn x{3})

Puts the selected bone's keys on its left / right pair as their mirror image, replacing the pair's keys, as one undo step. The clip's own motion isn't mirrored: the same fix is made on the other side.
This bone has no left / right pair (a centre bone).
Nothing to mirror: the bone needs keys, {0} needs a track in this clip, and the two can't both be selected.
Mirror keys of {0} to the other side on {1}
{0} bones selected (Ctrl+click): keys, Clear Keys, Copy Offset and the gizmo act on all of them, each in its own parent's space.
Copies {0}'s offset at frame {1}, to paste as a key at another frame or on another clip.
Copies the offset of every keyed bone (and the root) at frame {0}: a whole fix, to paste onto another clip such as the other _hi / _md / _lo variant.

Keys the offsets copied from {0} frame {1} ({2}) at frame {3} of this clip, each on the bone of the same name, as one undo step. An offset adds to the clip's own pose, so the same change is made to this clip.
{0} copied offsets weren't pasted on {1}: it has no track for {2}.
A weapon in each hand of the player character, held where its weapon param puts it, to judge arm edits against. Time act weapon moves (sheathing, two-handing) show in the Time Act Editor only.
More not shown: filter to narrow the list.
The selected bone's path over the whole clip, in orange, with a small cross at each of its keys: shows the arc of a swing and where it jumps. Shown with Show Skeleton on.
Faint skeletons of the clip some frames before (red) and after (green) the playing frame, to see the motion's arcs and spot pops. Shown with Show Skeleton on.
Onion skin skeletons on each side of the playing frame.
A second skeleton, in violet, plays another version of the clip alongside the edited one, at the same frame.
The clip as the project's anibnd has it: what it was before the work not exported yet. A new ID compares with the clip it was made from.
The clip as the game's own files have it, however often it has been exported since. A new ID compares with the clip it was made from.
The selected clip has no such version to compare with.
Couldn't read the game's version of {0} to compare with.
How large the joint spheres are drawn, times their default (a hundredth of the skeleton's height). Clicking a joint selects its bone.
{0} offset keys on {1} bones (kept apart by Save; applied when played, exported or given an operation)
Select a bone to move or turn it in the viewport.
The selected bone. The viewport gizmo is on it, at the playing frame.
This clip doesn't animate this bone, so it can't be keyed: a clip only animates the bones its binding lists.

Drag the gizmo in the viewport to move or turn this bone at the playing frame (Move or Rotate below), or type the offset in the fields. Each drag or Apply adds or changes the key at that frame. One key moves the bone for the whole clip; a zero key on each side limits it to a range.
The clip's root motion: how the game moves the character while it plays. Select it to key it with the gizmo and the fields, as a bone.

Drag the gizmo (on the root path's arrow) to move the root at the playing frame, or turn it about the up axis. The game moves the character by how much the root changes from frame to frame, so a lone key does nothing in game: put zero keys at the first and last frame and key the change between them (a hop, a side step).
This clip has no root motion: the first key gives it some, from standing in place.
How far the root is turned at this frame, in degrees about the up axis, on top of the clip's own turn.
How far the root is moved at this frame (X, Y up, Z), on top of the clip's own root motion.
Set the viewport gizmo to {0} ({1} while the viewport or this window is focused).
How far the bone is turned from the clip's own pose at this frame, in degrees about its parent's X, then Y, then Z axis.
How far the bone is moved from the clip's own pose at this frame, along its parent's X, Y and Z axes.
Set these as the key at this frame (adding the key if there is none). Can be undone.
Fill the fields again with the bone's offset at this frame, dropping what was typed.
How every bone's offset goes from one key to the next in this clip.
Add a key with no offset at the playing frame, so the bone is as the clip has it there. Put one on each side of a key to limit its effect to that range.
Shortcuts: {0} first frame, {1} playing frame, {2} last frame.
Make a new animation from this clip as it is now, exported next to it in the same anibnd. The original keeps its own ID and content.
Add the clip under this name (aXXX_YYYYYY), listed as (new) until exported. Can be undone.
A clip's name is aXXX_YYYYYY, such as a000_003500.
{0} is already a clip of this character.
A new ID also needs a time act entry (Time Act Editor) for its events, and a behavior clip for the game to play it.

Makes this ID's time act entry in the Time Act Editor, with the events of {0}'s entry, as one step of its undo history. The entry plays this clip, not {0}'s. Save the time acts there to keep it. Undo here doesn't undo it there.
{0}, which this clip was made from, has no time act entry to copy. Make one in the Time Act Editor.
Time act entry asked for in the Time Act Editor. Save the time acts there, then Read Time Acts Again on the Timeline.
Open the Behavior Editor's Register dialog for this clip's ID, to add the clip generator the game plays it through. The Behavior Editor saves its own file.
{0} couldn't be read, so its clips weren't exported.
{0} isn't in {1} any more, so it wasn't exported.
Animation Editor: saved the work of {0} clip(s) to {1}.
Failed to save the animation work in {0}
Failed to read the animation work file {0}
Failed to read the saved work of {0} in {1}. Its files are kept.
The saved work of {0} was made from {1}, which this character no longer has, so it wasn't opened. Its files are kept.
The saved keys on bone {0} of {1} were left out: the clip has no track for that bone.
Open a character to retarget clips onto it.
Where the clips come from: a character of this project, or of another stored project of any game whose animations can be read (DS3 into ER, for example). The other project is only read.
Another project's files are opened on the side, which can take a moment for the archive games.
The project's files couldn't be opened: {0}
This is the open character's own set ({0}). Pick another character.

Which source bone each bone of the open character follows. Bones are matched by name (spaces, underscores and L_ / _L written alike), and the other side of a bone picked by hand is matched for you. Bones without a source bone keep their reference pose. Picks are kept for this pair of characters.
{0} of {1} bones matched: {2} same name, {3} similar name, {4} mirrored, {5} by hand
Forget the bones picked by hand for this pair and match by name again.
How big the source's moves are made, and which clip of the open character the new clips are written through.
The source's moves (the pelvis bobbing, root motion) are scaled by the open character's size over the source's, measured at the hips. Bones keep the open character's own lengths either way.
Carry the source's root motion over (scaled). Off: the clips have none.

A new clip is written through a clip of the open character: it animates the bones that clip animates and goes into its anibnd. For an ID of another category the first clip of that category is used. A clip that replaces one keeps that clip's own.
{0} matched bones aren't animated by the template and stay at rest
The source clips to retarget, each under its own ID in the open character. DS1, DS1R and DES names (a01_3000) become a001_003000.
Replace: the open character's clip takes the retargeted motion. Skip: it is left alone. Next Free ID: the clip goes under the next unused ID of its category.
Retargets the picked clips onto the open character as one undo step. Save and Export as for any edit. A new ID still needs a time act entry (Clip tool).
Retarget passed over {0} clips (no ID, skipped, no free ID or no template): {1}
Another character was opened while retargeting, so the clips weren't added.
The retarget bone map {0} couldn't be read; starting from an empty one.
The retarget bone map {0} couldn't be written.

Moves Master, and so the whole pose, by this much on every frame, in metres. For a source that holds Master higher or lower than suits this skeleton (feet floating or sunk into the floor): raise or lower Y, retarget, and undo to try another value. Kept for this pair of characters.

Per clip, also moves Master up or down so it is at this skeleton's rest height on the first frame, then keeps that shift for the whole clip. The offset is added on top. Leave off for clips that start in the air.
The template animates no bone the offset can move
